g.text: text width is measured, never guessed
one call: authorDiagram — skeleton in, gated files out
author.js composes everything; geometry.js is shared
arrowBetween leaves 10 px at each end — the arrow owns the gap
Structure: parseable document, known element types, no duplicate ids, no
dangling bindings, image bytes present. Geometry (rotation-aware): frames
don't overlap, text fits its container, nothing escapes or squats on a frame, free
texts don't collide, arrows don't cross strangers, arrowheads land outside their
target. Style: 4.5:1 contrast, no text over images, house fonts only.

assets are bytes in the document, not paths
spliceLibraryItem regenerates every id — place the same item twice, no collision
dark is a filter, and it does not preserve contrast
dark = invert(93%) hue-rotate(180deg) — one CSS filter over the light colours
"ink / artifact" clears 4.5:1 in light (5.3) and drops to 2.2 dark — check.js scores both themes, so the gate catches it
four commands run the whole loop
the generator is the source of truth — withAuthoring measures, gates
and writes the .excalidraw and its SVG
re-prove any file: exit 0 clean, 1 defects, 2 unreadable; contrast is scored
SVG plus one PNG per frame in reading order; iterate with --frame N,
